Fastball: Coming out of college sitting in the low 90's with his fastball, Ashby is now throwing mid upper 90's consistently with some serious sink. There have been some jaw dropping pitches in his time in the majors and it's generating a ton of ground balls. He mixes a rare 4FB in as well, and I'd like him to continue to do that. Think it could be a nice putaway pitch for him at times.

 Slider: The slider is looking like an absolutely elite pitch for Ashby. Since his debut, there has only been one hit off of the slider and it was an infield hit. It's generating a whiff rate of 44.7% and a xWOBA of 0.114. This is the type of pitch that can carry an entire repertoire. 

 Changeup: The changeup is a pitch that Ashby developed in pro ball and it has come around to look like a very solid, major league pitch. Ashby is generating whiffs on 26.5% of the changeup's he's thrown in MLB, though he hasn't been able to master it as a ""put away"" pitch yet, having only struck out one batter on the change. 

 Curveball: The curve has not been used a ton in MLB and the results aren't great, but I think it's a decent enough pitch, especially when it's the 3rd best secondary. Brandon Woodruff's curve wouldn't be considered a great pitch, but it does the job as his fourth offering. That should be the goal for Ashby as well.
 
 Command will be what ultimately decides whether Ashby can be a MLB starter. It comes and goes at the moment. Because of this Jekyll and Hyde situation with his command, there's definitely some risk that Ashby is a reliever long term. But even if that's the case, he's still probably a high leverage, multi inning relief weapon. Brewers fans know as well as anybody, how valuable that type of pitcher can be. The good news is, that he still has shown an ability to avoid walking batters as a major leaguer. It's more of an issue of commanding where in the zone his pitches will end up, than it is of him commanding his pitches into the strike zone in general.

Physical Description Report: Smaller in stature, sturdy lower half, very little projection left, if any.
Hit / Mechanics Report: Stretch only. Front foot slightly open, which is an interesting starting point. Throws from a low 3/4 slot. Average extension, but low release height, due in part to his own height, but also a drop and drive motion.
Power/Pitch 1 Report: Sitting 92-94 and has topped at 95.2 MPH in MLB in 2026. Low release helps give it a flat VAA of -4.18 to go along with an impressive 18" of IVB from that height. He commands the pitch very well. This is a borderline plus pitch and should get quite a bit of whiff when he gets it up in the zone or above.
Run/Pitch 2 Report: His top whiff pitch, the changeup is averaging around 20" of armside run this season, though some of the depth has gone away, sitting in the 6" range and not getting lower than 4.4" of IVB, when he was all the way down under 1" of IVB at times last year. Still a really good pitch, but maybe not quite as effective against righties with this change to the profile. Command has been more touch and go this year, leaving it up more often, but the pitch is a plus offering overall still.
Field/Pitch 3 Report: On its own, a pretty mediocre offering that is hovering around 0" of gloveside movement on average. Solid bridge pitch for him though, capable of getting early contact for outs, and he's commanded it at an average or better level so far in 2026. More consistency with the shape would go a long way, because there are some good flashes.
Arm/Pitch 4 Report: Henderson seems to have finally found a true breaking ball. He's only thrown 9 of them so far this year, but they're averaging 16" of gloveside movement and sitting in sweeper or slurve territory more than a true slider. Either way, it's an above average pitch now that could be a good swing-and-miss pitch against righties, especially because he's commanded it really well in the small sample. They should use it more than they have so far.
Summary Report: Henderson is close to graduating from prospect status, but he looks like Top 100 guy and a potential mid-rotation starter now that he's finally figured out some glove-side weapons. It's been a slow-burn, and he's one that deals with a lot of injuries, so you still need to keep an eye on that, but he seems to be locking up a big-league rotation spot at this point. He will find quite a bit of success with his bulldog attitude, and with the current pitch mix and command he's showed in MLB so far.
